issueContext.title: CRI getFsInfo logs errors for valid filesystems mounted after kubelet start
issueContext.body:
**What happened**:

New overlay filesystems created for Pods after kubelet start trigger repeated error messages. For example:

```
cri_stats_provider.go:375] Failed to get the info of the filesystem with mountpoint "/var/lib/containers/storage/overlay/2243263dc8ba6c55d8867d3e47bcaaa145d15f0ace19420824d639d86defe2e3/merged": failed to get device for dir "/var/lib/containers/storage/overlay/2243263dc8ba6c55d8867d3e47bcaaa145d15f0ace19420824d639d86defe2e3/merged": could not find device with major: 0, minor: 83 in cached partitions map.
```

Error messages are logged every 10 seconds for every filesystem created after kubelet start. For large kubelet nodes, this issue creates an excessive amount of error logs.

**What you expected to happen**:

New overlay filesystems created for Pods after kubelet start should not log error messages.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Use cri_stats_provider with cri-o and configure overlay storage. UsingLegacyCadvisorStats() needs to return false per https://github.com/cri-o/cri-o/pull/3054 for cri_stats_provider to be used. Start with an empty /var/lib/containers/storage and schedule Pods on the node.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

As part of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/59475, cadvisor.GetFsInfoByFsUUID() was changed to cadvisor.GetDirFsInfo() in getFsInfo(); however, the test for cadvisorfs.ErrNoSuchDevice was not modified, changing how getFsInfo() handles a cache miss from cadvisor. 

cadvisor caches UUIDs/partitions/mounts on kubelet start and the cache is never refreshed. Given that it's expected that getFsInfo() will fail to retrieve data from cadvisor (see comments in ImageFsStats() and https://github.com/kubernetes/heapster/issues/1793), this condition should not be logged as an error. Alternatively, cadvisor fs could be modified to refresh on cache miss enabling getFsInfo() to return data on these filesystems.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes ver

issueContext.title: pod_status_manager_state: checkpoint is corrupted
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

After enabling In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling, if deploy a pod without setting memory (or cpu) request, kubelet will be failed at its second restart


### What did you expect to happen?

kubelet restart successfully

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. start kubelet with In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling enabled
2. deploy a pod without setting memory request, e.g: 
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - image: nginx:1.24.0
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    name: nginx
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 100m
```
3. restart kubelet for the first time
4. restart kubelet for the second time
5. kubelet will fail with error: `panic: could not restore state from checkpoint: checkpoint is corrupted, please drain this node and delete pod allocation checkpoint file "/var/lib/kubelet/pod_status_manager_state" before restarting Kubelet` 

### Anything else we need to know?

After deploying the pod, the following information is saved in the file `pod_status_manager_state`:

```
      "nginx": {
        "cpu": "100m"
      }
```
Then restart kubelet for the first time, the relevant content in the file becomes: 
```
      "nginx": {
        "cpu": "100m",
        "memory": "0"
      }
```
------
When deploying the pod, as there are no records in the checkpoint (`pod_status_manager_state`), kubelet will get resource config from `pod.Spec.Container.Resources`  directly and save it to the checkpoint (without memory request)
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3125009dd1ebdde499a810110ba1f6d3fb05698f/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L2504-L2521
When restarting kubelet for the first time, it will restore the previously saved data from the checkpoint. Since the memory request was not previously set, it will be set to an empty value and resaved to the checkpoint
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3125009dd1ebdde499a810110ba1f6d3fb05698

issueContext.body:
### What happened?

Currently kube-proxy efficiently cleans all stale conntrack entries preventing traffic black holing for deleted endpoints, but there can be some corner cases when conntrack cleaning happens before programming the network leaving a small window in which if any packet arrives will back-hole the traffic.

The corner case:
Taking a simple case of load-balancer service backed by a deployment with single replica, on deleting the pod(gracefully), I observed two **OnEndpointSliceUpdate** invocations:
1.  First one with EndpointConditions.Ready as false
2. EndpointSlice was cleared for the pod

1. issueContext.title: Kubelet creates leases without ownerReference set if node doesn't exist
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

* Some external controller deleted node object while kubelet was alive
* Due to ignoring errors in kubelet's lease logic, it created lease without ownerReference set

### What did you expect to happen?

* Kubelet doesn't create lease without ownerReference set in any case, even pathological one

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

* Some external controller deletes node object
* Garbage collector properly deletes associated lease object
* Kubelet tries to update object and it fails on Conflict (saying that UID doesn't match): 
  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b1e130fe83156783153538b6d79821c2fdaa85bb/staging/src/k8s.io/component-helpers/apimachinery/lease/controller.go#L179-L198
* We go to `apierrors.IsConflict(err)` branch, call backoffEnsureLease and assign result to base, but backoffEnsureLease may return potentially invalid object if ensureLease returned error (which happens when newLeasePostProcessFunc returns error, e.g. when node doesn't exist).
* We `continue`
* The next loop calls c.newLease on the incorrect base and ignores error in line 181 (so the second attempt to call newLeasePostProcessFunc which also fails with an error) 
* We do UPDATE with incomplete (without effect of newLeasePostProcessFunc) object
* Given that leases allow CreateOnUpdate a new object, without ownerReference is created: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b1e130fe83156783153538b6d79821c2fdaa85bb/pkg/registry/coordination/lease/strategy.go#L65-L68

issueContext.title: sched: CycleState.SkipFilterPlugins not always injected into cycleState
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

In k8s 1.27, scheduler introduced a new "short circuit" semantics in PreFilter to bypass a Pod quickly. A change introduced here is it relies on that plugin to be stored in `CycleState.SkipFilterPlugins`, which makes sense as what it was explained [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/114125/files#r1062646736).

However, the `SkipFilterPlugins` info, although is populated upon each plugin's PreFilter invocation, is not injected into `CycleState` when some PreFilter returns unschedulable:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L655-L661

So think about this workflow:

- pluginA returns Skip in its PreFilter
- pluginB return Unschedulable in its PreFilter
- note: pluginA is not included in `CycleState.SkipFilterPlugins` due to aforementioned bug
- a Pod is claimed as unschedulable (failed by pluginB)
- during PostFilter, it's **supposed** to bypass pluginA's PreEnqueueExtension's AddPod/RemovePod, but it doesn't
- calling a "skipped" Plugin's AddPod/RemovePod during preemption, sometimes will abort the whole preemption as the logic tries to read info from cycleState, and some plugin's "skip" version doesn't fill cycleState properly, e.g., InterPodAffinity (skip immediately w/o write preFilterStateKey).

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/interpodaffinity/filtering.go#L257-L262

### What did you expect to happen?

Short circuiting using Skip is fine, but `CycleState.SkipFilterPlugins` should injected properly at all cases.

Described in the workflow above.

issueContext.title: Service `status.loadBalancer.ingress` can be set when `type` != `LoadBalancer`
issueContext.body:
xref 119454

I think this may be one of the few cases where we can actually change the behavior in a "breaking" way.

User creates service with `.type=ClusterIP`, `.status.loadBalancer` is empty
Controller or user updates the status subresource, sets `.spec.loadBalancer.ingress[].ip` (not wiped or validated, should be)
User updates `service spec` in any way, `.staus.loadBalancer` is wiped

It's clear that the `.status.loadBalancer` is not meant to be set when `.type` is not "LoadBalancer".

The question is:

1) Fail validation?
2) Silently discard the value?
3) Warn and then discard the value?
4) Just warn and leave it.

Because we allowed it in the past, but it is so volatile, I lean towards 3.

@aojea and @khenidak - the people most familair with this type.

Edit: PrepareForUpdate() runs before warnings.  So:

(1) is easy
(2) is easy
(4) is slightly less easy than (2)
(3) is slightly less easy than (4)

issueContext.title: Can't restrict access from K8s nodes with loadBalancerSourceRanges for proxy-mode=ipvs
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

When using loadBalancerSourceRanges to allow access only from CIDRs outside the cluster segment, access from the K8s nodes (or pods with hostNetwork:true) should be rejected, but for proxy-mode=ipvs it works.

/sig network
/area kube-proxy
/area ipvs

### What did you expect to happen?

Access from K8s nodes should be rejected in the same way as for proxy-mode=iptables

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Define a service with loadBalancerSourceRanges that allows access from a cidr outside the cluster, e.g.

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: alpine
spec:
  loadBalancerSourceRanges:
#  - "192.168.1.0/24"
  - "192.168.2.0/24"
#  - "fd00::c0a8:100/120"
  - "fd00::c0a8:200/120"
  ipFamilyPolicy: RequireDualStack
  selector:
    app: alpine
  type: LoadBalancer
  allocateLoadBalancerNodePorts: false
  ports:
  - port: 5001
    name: nc
```
The K8s nodes have addresses on 192.168.1.0/24 and fd00::c0a8:100/120.

Make sure a loadBalancerIP is assigned (in this example 10.0.0.0/32) and try to access it from a K8s node:
```
# With proxy.mode=ipvs
> nc 10.0.0.0:5001
alpine-f6c8bd7db-zljnl    # (works)
# With proxy.mode=iptables
# nc 10.0.0.0:5001
# (hangs...)
```

### Anything else we need to know?

Same for both ipv4 and ipv6.

This is related to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119524 since a fix requires that the `nodeID` passed to the `kube-proxy` is correct. Please see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119524#issuecomment-1655389139

### Kubernetes version

v1.27.4 and master

None

### OS version

Linux 6.4.4

None

issueContext.title: Remove tracking finalizers from Pods belonging to finished Jobs
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

When a Job is deleted (via Background cascade), we have a backup logic to remove finalizers from pods

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f0dcf0614036d8c3cd1c9f3b3cf8df4bb1d8e44e/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L513-L518

This logic could also be applied for any finished Job.

### Why is this needed?

While investigating a case similar to #119159, we observed that the job controller didn't delete finalizers from Pods where the Job was deleted with Foreground cascading policy.

Since the Job was already marked as Finished, it only makes sense to trigger the backup logic to remove finalizers, so that we can guard against any possible bug where a Job is marked as Finished but not all pod finalizers are removed.

Note that I'm not aware of any other bug in tracking with finalizers.

issueContext.title: [KCCM]: service update while node sync is processing might impact ingress
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

The Kubernetes cloud controller manager uses resource watchers to sync load balancers, a Node/Service watcher. The Node watcher is slower by nature since any Node event will sync all service load balancers on the cluster. The service watcher is quicker since it only syncs the service load balancer which the event relates to. 

How slow a Node sync is will vary on the cluster, i.e: amount of Services of `type: LoadBalancer` and Nodes, but on big clusters with a lot of churn: the time to process one Node sync can be sufficiently slow to have the cache of Nodes go stale w.r.t the actual cluster state. The cache of Nodes is here the resource informer cache. When syncing Nodes the Node control loop will list all Nodes in its cache and then iterate over all Services and sync their load balancers in parallel, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L799-L818

If any Service experiences an update needing a load balancer sync, the Service controller will also list the Nodes in the informer cache, but retrieve a more up-to-date copy, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L438-L451. 

During upgrades or similar operations where a lot of Nodes get added/deleted: it's rather easy for the following to occur;

1. Node sync is processing, N load balancers are synced
2. NodeY is added

issueContext.body:
### What happened?

In 1.26 the service controller in the Kubernetes cloud controller manage (KCCM) introduced a new mechanism for syncing load balancers based on predicates. issueContext.title: Introduce `MatchLabelKeys` (the same one as Pod Topology Spread) to `PodAffinityTerm`
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Introduce `MatchLabelKeys` to [PodAffinityTerm](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/api/core/v1#PodAffinityTerm) (like [we do to Pod Topology Spread](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-scheduling/3243-respect-pod-topology-spread-after-rolling-upgrades)).

### Why is this needed?

Currently, the scheduler doesn’t treat `Terminating` Pods as removed Pods.
See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/105661. Pod Topology Spreading gets imbalanced after Deployment/Replicaset upgrades because of that. So, we introduced `MatchLabelKeys` to Pod Topology Spread (https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3243).

In Pod Affinity and Pod Anti Affinity, it gives a negative impact on the scheduling result to take old Pods into account during scheduling (“Old Pods” = Pods from a old deployment); Old pods may result in filtering out Nodes that should have gone to the Scoring phase (in `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution`), or giving low scores to Nodes that should have been given higher scores. (in `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution`).

/sig scheduling

issueContext.title: kube-proxy: Drop packets in INVALID state drops packets from outside the pod range
issueContext.body:
**What happened**:
When kube-proxy is configured with a cluster-cidr range, it drops packets with an INVALID conntrack state for all sources on the KUBE-FORWARD chain. This is meant to prevent spurious retransmits in long-lived TCP connections to a service IP, but it prevents clusters from having asymmetrical routing on private subnets with services outside of a cluster. 

**What you expected to happen**:
Packets on the KUBE-FORWARD chain with an INVALID conntrack state should be dropped for only sources inside of the cluster-cidr if set.

issueContext.title: node.status.nodeInfo.kubeProxyVersion is a lie
issueContext.body:
`v1.Node` has a field `.status.nodeInfo.kubeProxyVersion`, about which [the API docs](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.0/staging/src/k8s.io/api/core/v1/types.go#L5250) say:

```
// KubeProxy Version reported by the node.
KubeProxyVersion string `json:"kubeProxyVersion" protobuf:"bytes,8,opt,name=kubeProxyVersion"`
```

but the field is [set by kubelet](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.0/pkg/kubelet/nodestatus/setters.go#L401), which does not actually know the kube-proxy version:

```
node.Status.NodeInfo.KubeletVersion = version.Get().String()
// TODO: kube-proxy might be different version from kubelet in the future
node.Status.NodeInfo.KubeProxyVersion = version.Get().String()
```

Not only is it possible that the kube-proxy version is different from the kubelet version, it's also possible that kube-proxy isn't even running on the machine.

This field should be marked as deprecated. Ideally kubelet would stop setting it but that might be considered an API break? If kubelet is going to continue setting it, then the API docs and the kubelet source should both be updated to indicate that the field is just an alias for `kubeletVersion` and does not actually indicate the kube-proxy version, and will be set even if kube-proxy is not running.

(Noticed by @liggitt)

/sig node
/sig network

`kube-proxy` now has a new nftables-based mode, available by running

    `kube-proxy --feature-gates NFTablesProxyMode=true --proxy-mode nftables`

This is currently an alpha-level feature and while it probably will not
eat your data, it may nibble at it a bit. (It passes e2e testing but has
not yet seen real-world use.)

At this point it should be functionally mostly identical to the iptables
mode, except that it does not (and will not) support Service NodePorts on
127.0.0.1. (Also note that there are currently no command-line arguments
for the nftables-specific config; you will need to use a config file if
you want to set the equivalent of any of the `--iptables-xxx` options.)

As this code is still very new, it has not been heavily optimized yet;
while it is expected to _eventually_ have better performance than the
iptables backend, very little performance testing has been done so far.

Upgrade kubernetes to `v1.27.3` and install a container that uses uses apiserver aggregation such as `calico` or `kubevirt`.

https://github.com/k3s-io/k3s/issues/8038

issueContext.title: scheduler: register default EventsToRegister in only some extension points
issueContext.body:
## What

register default EventsToRegister only for PreFilter, Filter, Reserve, and Permit plugins.

Currently, we register default EventsToRegister for all plugins that don't have EnqueueExtension.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L551-L554

## Why

EventsToRegister affects which events the scheduler watches, and when registered events come, the scheduling queue requeue Pods according to them. The queue checks the event can make Pod schedulable or not via QueueingHint from pInfo.UnschedulablePlugins.
Given this fact, plugins that never be registered in pInfo.UnschedulablePlugins don't need to have EventsToRegister. 
And, currently, only PreFilter, Filter, Reserve, and Permit affect pInfo.UnschedulablePlugins. Meaning all other plugins' EventsToRegister actually don't affect anything, and to register default EventsToRegister to other plugins could result in watching events in vain, which all of PreFilter, Filter, Reserve, and Permit plugins aren't interested in.

/kind feature
/sig scheduling

issueContext.title: VolumeZone scheduling plugin should handle csi migration
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

In https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114268, we discovered that our plan for eventually removing the [VolumeZone](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/volumezone) scheduling plugin when CSI migration is GA is not possible because the plugin also applies to non-migratable volume types.

However, if we leave the plugin as is, then even migratable PVs will be broken if we remove beta topology labels from Nodes in the future. This is because the plugin does not have any handling for migrated volumes.


### What did you expect to happen?

I suggest we add CSI migration handling to the VolumeZone plugin. I think we just need to detect if the volume is migrated, and if so, skip the VolumeZone processing. For migrated volumes, we translate `PV.Labels` into `PV.NodeAffinity` so they end up getting processed by the [VolumeBinding](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/volumebinding) plugin.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

In a cluster with csi migration for a specific intree volume type enabled,
1. create an intree PV with beta topology labels
2. remove the beta topology label from a node
3. try to schedule a pod using that pv

### What happened?

Running containers in privileged mode is not recommended as privileged containers run with all [linux capabilities](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/capabilities.7.html) enabled and can access the host's resources. Running containers in privileged mode opens number of security threads such as breakout to underlying host OS.

Currently the kube-proxy DaemonSet runs in privileged mode.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/863a462eeccca4c24bf4c4e9012f5ebccade70a2/cluster/addons/kube-proxy/kube-proxy-ds.yaml#L50-L51

https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/kubelet-in-userns/#configuring-kube-proxy describes how to run kube-proxy in "rootless". To my understanding "rootless" != non-privileged mode but this configuration can be also used for running in non-privileged mode. However I see that following issues with it:
1. In the provided kube-proxy component config in https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/kubelet-in-userns/#configuring-kube-proxy we have to disable certain settins to prevent kube-proxy from ensuring sysctls (which is allowed only in privileged container).

But when I tried to run kube-proxy with the provided component config it fails because it tries to ensure yet another syctl:
```
F0818 08:03:55.514875       1 server.go:494] unable to create proxier: unable to create ipv4 proxier: can't set sysctl net/ipv4/conf/all/route_localnet to 1: open /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/all/route_localnet: read-only file system
```

It is `net/ipv4/conf/all/route_localnet` that is being set in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/58c10aa6eb5adfb1f3aa4d6cb898b8c347ba9e72/pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go#L263-L265

And I don't see a way how to disable kube-proxy from ensuring this sysctl from its component config.

2. In general the whole approach that explicitly sets 0 values to prevent kube-proxy from ensuring syctls seems not a sustainable one. The long lived kube-proxy container should be abl

issueContext.title: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy: variable expression type not recognized as return type in expression that evaluates the variable
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Variables field is added to ValidatingAdmissionPolicy in 1.28. Currently the usage of variables would expect a operator associated. 
e.g. (thanks to Mariam Fahmy for raising the issue)
```
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: "chech-deployment-labels"
spec:
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups:   ["apps"]
      apiVersions: ["v1"]
      operations:  ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
      resources:   ["deployments"]
  variables:
    - name: environment
      expression: "has(object.metadata.labels) && 'env' in object.metadata.labels && object.metadata.labels['env'] == 'prod'"
  validations:
    - expression: "variables.environment"
      message: "Deployment labels must be env=prod"
```
Above will fail with error: 
```
The ValidatingAdmissionPolicy "chech-deployment-labels" is invalid: spec.validations[0].expression: Invalid value: "variables.environment": must evaluate to bool
```
Meanwhile the `- expression: "variables.environment == true"` will pass.

The reason is when variables be evaluated to non dyn type(like bool or string), it will require special handling(like casting) since we use dyn type everywhere. 

### Why is this needed?

It might confuse user.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a bug on the endpoints controller that does not reconcile the Endpoint object after this is truncated (it gets more than 1000 endpoints addresses)
bugOrRegression.author: aojea

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a kubelet and kube-apiserver memory leak in default 1.29 configurations related to tracing.
bugOrRegression.author: dashpole

bugOrRegression.description:
Fixes a regression introduced in 1.29 where conntrack entries for UDP connections
  to deleted pods did not get cleaned up correctly, which could (among other things)
  cause DNS problems when DNS pods were restarted.
bugOrRegression.author: danwinship

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix wrong member list reported when removing an etcd member
bugOrRegression.author: SataQiu

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: when adding new control plane nodes with "kubeadm join", ensure that the etcd member addition is performed only if a given member URL does not already exist in the list of members. Similarly, on "kubeadm reset" only remove an etcd member if its ID exists.
bugOrRegression.author: SataQiu

bugOrRegression.description:
The scheduling queue didn't notice any extenders' failures, it could miss some cluster events,
  and it could end up Pods rejected by Extenders stuck in unschedulable pod pool in 5min in the worst-case scenario.
  Now, the scheduling queue notices extenders' failures and requeue Pods rejected by Extenders appropriately.
bugOrRegression.author: sanposhiho

other.description: Kubeadm: removed `socat` and `ebtables` from kubeadm preflight checks
other.author: saschagrunert

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a bug when the hostname label of a node does not match the node name, pods bound to a PV with nodeAffinity using the hostname may be scheduled to the wrong node or experience scheduling failures.
bugOrRegression.author: AxeZhan

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a suboptimal scheduler preemption behavior where potential preemption victims were violating Pod Disruption Budgets.
bugOrRegression.author: NoicFank

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.9
feature.author: cpanato

securityFixes.title: Command Injection affecting Windows nodes via nodes/*/logs/query API
securityFixes.description:
A security vulnerability has been discovered in Kubernetes windows nodes
that could allow a user with the ability to query a node's '/logs' endpoint
to execute arbitrary commands on the host.
